+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""FINDING F1 (P0): in-place assign with a backward-shifted self-read (via PAD, or via
+SHRINK/roll on a whole-buffer target) compiles to a single kernel that reads and writes
+the same buffer with no staging -> wrong results on CPU under default flags.
+
+Found: 2026-06-10, HEAD 6e1b61f16. Oracle: CPU vs METAL (S2/ASSIGN sweep) + numpy value
+semantics. NOT a recent regression: same wrong output at ac079e43d (2026-02-16) and
+d1cce7a47 (fix_store_hazard introduction, #15759, 2026-04-16).
+
+Expected (value semantics, eval-RHS-then-store — the contract that
+test/unit/test_assign.py:439 test_overlapping_shrink_assignment_forward/_reverse pin
+for shrunken TARGETS):       [0, 1, 2, ..., 15]   (shift-right-by-one of arange(1,17))
+Actual CPU (default opts):   [0, 1, 2, 3, 3, 5, 6, 7, 7, 9, 10, 11, 11, 13, 14, 15]
+                              (wrong at i=4,8,12: each float4 block reads the previous
+                               block's last element AFTER it was overwritten)
+Actual CPU (NOOPT=1):        [0, 0, 0, ..., 0]   (serial cascade of the pad zero)
+Actual METAL:                correct -- by thread-scheduling luck; same unsynchronized
+                              read/write, so it is UB there too.
+
+Suspected mechanism: tinygrad/schedule/rangeify.py fix_store_hazard (:91-98).
+  unsafe = {Ops.PERMUTE, Ops.FLIP} | ({Ops.SHRINK} if target.op_in_backward_slice_with_self(Ops.SHRINK) else set())
+- PAD is never in `unsafe`, so a pad-shifted self-read inserts no .contiguous() staging.
+- SHRINK is only unsafe when the TARGET is shrunken; whole-buffer targets with a
+  shifted SHRINK on the RHS (e.g. Tensor.roll = repeat+shrink) slip through too.
+- Contrast: tinygrad/schedule/indexing.py:23 realize_store_after_src checks
+  (SHRINK, PERMUTE, FLIP, PAD) -- including PAD -- but only for COPY/SLICE sources.
+The generated kernel (DEBUG=4, NOOPT=1) is:
+    void E_16(float* restrict data0_16) {
+      for (int Lidx0 = 0; Lidx0 < 16; Lidx0++) {
+        float val0 = ((0<Lidx0)?*(data0_16+(Lidx0+-1)):0.0f);
+        *(data0_16+Lidx0) = val0;   // reads data0[i-1], writes data0[i]: hazard
+      }
+    }
+(also note `restrict` on a pointer that is both read and written at different offsets)
+
+Maintainers already suspect this hole exists: test/unit/test_assign.py:437
+  "# TODO: is there a way to sneak in a permute such that it returns the wrong answer?"
+Answer: not via permute (guarded) -- via PAD or roll.
+
+Dedupe: not in any @expectedFailure; no open gh issue found for assign+pad/roll/hazard.
+"""
+import numpy as np
+from tinygrad import Tensor
+
+def show(name, fn, npfn, n=16):
+  base = np.arange(1, n+1, dtype=np.float32)
+  exp = npfn(base.copy())
+  print(f"--- {name}   expected: {exp[:8]} ...")
+  for dev in ("CPU", "METAL"):
+    x = Tensor(base.copy(), device=dev).contiguous().realize()
+    fn(x)
+    got = x.numpy()
+    ok = np.allclose(got, exp, rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-5)
+    print(f"  {dev:6s} {'ok    ' if ok else 'WRONG '} {got[:8]} ...")
+
+# V1: pad-shifted self-read (minimal form of the bug)
+show("V1 pad shift-right", lambda x: x.assign(x.pad(((1, 0),))[:16] * 1.0),
+     lambda a: np.concatenate([[0.0], a[:-1]]).astype(np.float32))
+# V2: pure-movement RHS, same wrongness
+show("V2 pad shift, no ALU", lambda x: x.assign(x.pad(((1, 0),))[:16]),
+     lambda a: np.concatenate([[0.0], a[:-1]]).astype(np.float32))
+# V3: Tensor.roll -- the natural user-facing spelling (repeat+shrink internally)
+show("V3 roll(+1)", lambda x: x.assign(x.roll(1, 0)), lambda a: np.roll(a, 1))
+# V4: roll the other way; wraparound positions still read-behind
+show("V4 roll(-3)", lambda x: x.assign(x.roll(-3, 0)), lambda a: np.roll(a, -3))
+# control: flip IS guarded by fix_store_hazard (PERMUTE/FLIP in unsafe set)
+show("CTL flip (guarded, passes)", lambda x: x.assign(x.flip(0)), lambda a: a[::-1])

+"""FINDING F2 (P2 symptom, latent infra bug underneath): PCONTIG=3 crashes with
+`NameError: name 'AxisType' is not defined` on any graph that reaches the
+partial-contiguous branch of remove_bufferize. Crashes identically on CPU and METAL.
+
+Found: 2026-06-10, HEAD 6e1b61f16. Oracle: O5 PCONTIG ladder (flag-gated, experimental).
+
+Symptom site: tinygrad/schedule/rangeify.py:293 (inside remove_bufferize):
+    is_pcontig, is_subs = partition(subs, lambda x: x[0] in exclude_ranges or
+                                    any([r.arg[-1] == AxisType.REDUCE for r in x[1].ranges]))
+rangeify.py DOES import AxisType (line 5). The NameError comes from how
+PatternMatcher callbacks are rebuilt:
+
+Root cause: tinygrad/uop/ops.py:1331 deconstruct_function prunes a callback's
+globals to names found in fxn.__code__.co_names plus ONE level of nested code
+objects (the co_consts loop at :1333-1334 does not recurse). `AxisType` is
+referenced only inside a listcomp nested inside a lambda (depth 2). On Python
+3.11 (the repo's pinned version) a listcomp is its own code object, so the
+harvest misses it and the rebuilt remove_bufferize runs with globals lacking
+AxisType. On Python 3.12+ (PEP 709 comprehension inlining) the same code
+harvests fine -- version-dependent latency. Verified both ways:
+  3.11.15: deconstruct_function(remove_bufferize) globals: AxisType MISSING
+  3.12.13: AxisType present
+
+Blast radius: audited all 832 unique callbacks registered in PatternMatchers
+across tinygrad/ -- remove_bufferize is the ONLY one whose nested code
+references a module global missed by the depth-1 harvest. So today this is
+"PCONTIG=3 is fully broken"; structurally it is a trap for any future pattern.
+
+The line entered in 6df19a4ac (2025-10-23, #12887) -- latent ever since; CI has
+no PCONTIG runs (grep .github/workflows: no hits), which is why it never fired.
+
+Dedupe: no open issue mentions it; not in any xfail. NEW.
+NO FIX APPLIED (documentation only). Candidate fixes (for discussion, not done):
+recurse in deconstruct_function's harvest, or reference AxisType at depth<=1 in
